title.zh: 卷一百五十二 列傳第三十九: 張晉亨 王珍 楊傑只哥 劉通 岳存 張子良 唐慶 齊榮顯 石天祿 石抹阿辛 劉斌 趙柔
title.en: Volume 152 Biographies 39: Zhang Jinheng, Wang Zhen, Yang Jiezhige, Liu Tong, Yue Cun, Zhang Ziliang, Tang Qing, Qi Rongxian, Shi Tianlu, Shi Moaxin, Liu Bin, Zhao Rou
title.raw: 卷一百五十二 列傳第三十九: 張晉亨 王珍 楊傑只哥 劉通 岳存 張子良 唐慶 齊榮顯 石天祿 石抹阿辛 劉斌 趙柔 Volume 152 Biographies 39: Zhang Jinheng, Wang Zhen, Yang Jiezhige, Liu Tong, Yue Cun, Zhang Ziliang, Tang Qing, Qi Rongxian, Shi Tianlu, Shi Moaxin, Liu Bin, Zhao Rou

sentences.zh: 張晉亨好古

translations.literal: Zhang Jinheng; Haogu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinheng

sentences.zh: 張晉亨字進卿，冀州南宮人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jinheng, courtesy name Jinqing, was a man of Nangong in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinheng, whose courtesy name was Jinqing, came from Nangong in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 其兄同知安武軍節度使事、領棗強令顥，以冀州數道之衆，附嚴實于青崖，後從實來歸，進顥安武軍節度使，西征，戰沒。

translations.literal: His elder brother Hao, who served as associate commissioner of the Anwu Military Commission and concurrently held the post of magistrate of Zaoqiang, led the multitudes of Jizhou's several circuits to join Yan Shi at Qingya; later he followed Shi in submitting, Hao was promoted to Military Commissioner of Anwu, and on the western campaign he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Hao, who served as deputy commissioner of the Anwu Military Commission while also governing Zaoqiang, had rallied the forces of several Jizhou circuits to Yan Shi at Qingya. When Shi later came over to the Mongols, Hao was promoted to military commissioner of Anwu; he fell in battle on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 歲戊寅，太師、國王木華黎承制，署晉亨襲顥爵。

translations.literal: In the year wuyin, Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali, acting by imperial order, appointed Jinheng to succeed Hao in his title.
translations.idiomatic: In 1218, Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali, acting on imperial authority, had Jinheng inherit his brother's rank.

sentences.zh: 晉亨涉獵書史，小心畏慎，臨事周密，實器之，以女妻焉。

translations.literal: Jinheng ranged through books and histories, was cautious and fearful in conduct, thorough in handling affairs; Shi valued him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jinheng read widely in history and the classics, acted with careful restraint, and handled affairs with meticulous thoroughness. Yan Shi came to rely on him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 實征澤、潞，偏將李信、晁海相繼降于宋，晉亨跋涉險阻，晝伏夜行，僅免於難。

translations.literal: When Shi campaigned in Ze and Lu, the flank generals Li Xin and Chao Hai successively surrendered to Song; Jinheng trudged through dangers and obstacles, lay hidden by day and marched by night, and barely escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: During Shi's campaign in Ze and Lu, the flank commanders Li Xin and Chao Hai defected to the Song in turn. Jinheng made his way through rugged country, hiding by day and traveling by night, and only narrowly escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 實遣子忠貞入質，命晉亨與俱。

translations.literal: Shi sent his son Zhongzhen in as a hostage and ordered Jinheng to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi sent his son Zhongzhen to court as a hostage, he ordered Jinheng to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，從國王孛羅征益都，以功遷昭毅大將軍，領恩州刺史，兼行臺馬步軍都緫領，再遷鎮國大將軍。

translations.literal: In dinghai, he followed Prince Boluo in campaigning against Yidu; for merit he was transferred to Grand General of Manifest Valor, held the post of prefect of Enzhou, and concurrently served as overall commander of the Branch Secretariat's horse and foot forces; he was again promoted to Grand General Who Stabilizes the State.
translations.idiomatic: In 1227 he followed Prince Boluo in the conquest of Yidu. For his service he was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor, made prefect of Enzhou, and appointed overall commander of the branch secretariat's cavalry and infantry, and was later raised again to Grand General Who Stabilizes the State.

sentences.zh: 實征淮楚、河南，晉亨畢從。

translations.literal: When Shi campaigned in Huai-Chu and Henan, Jinheng followed him throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shi campaigned in the Huai region, Chu, and Henan, Jinheng went with him to the end.

sentences.zh: 甲午，從實入覲，命為東平路行軍千戶。

translations.literal: In jiawu, he followed Shi to audience and was appointed a campaign thousand-household of the Dongping Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1234 he accompanied Shi to an audience at court and was appointed a campaign thousand-household on the Dongping circuit.

sentences.zh: 圍安慶，其守將走，邀擊之，斬首百級，俘獲無筭。

translations.literal: Besieging Anqing, its defending general fled; he intercepted and struck him, beheaded heads in the hundreds, and captives and booty were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Anqing the defending commander fled; Jinheng intercepted him, took more than a hundred heads, and captured prisoners and booty beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 攻光之定城，俘其將士十有五人。

translations.literal: Attacking Dingcheng in Guang, he captured fifteen of its officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Dingcheng in Guang prefecture he took fifteen enemy officers and men prisoner.

sentences.zh: 略信陽，執復州將金之才。

translations.literal: Raids on Xinyang; he seized the Fuzhou general Jin Zhicai.
translations.idiomatic: On a raid into Xinyang he captured the Fuzhou commander Jin Zhicai.

sentences.zh: 攻六安，拔之。

translations.literal: Attacking Lu'an, he took it.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Lu'an and captured it.

sentences.zh: 大小數十戰，策功居多。

translations.literal: In several dozen battles large and small, his counted merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: In dozens of engagements large and small, his recorded achievements ranked among the highest.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，李璮叛，晉亨從嚴忠範戰於遙牆濼，勝之，改本道奧魯萬戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Li Tan rebelled; Jinheng followed Yan Zhongfan in battle at Yaojiangpo and defeated him; he was changed to auruq ten-thousand-household of this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262, when Li Tan rebelled, Jinheng followed Yan Zhongfan to battle at Yaojiang Marsh and won. He was then reassigned as the circuit's auruq ten-thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 四年，授金虎符，分將本道兵充萬戶，戍宿州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was granted a gold tiger tally, divided command of this circuit's troops as ten-thousand-household, and garrisoned Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he received a gold tiger tally, took command of part of the circuit's forces as a ten-thousand-household, and was posted to garrison Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 首言：「汴堤南北，沃壤閒曠，宜屯田以資軍食。」

translations.literal: He was first to say: "North and south of the Bian embankment, the fertile soil lies open and idle; garrison farming should be established to supply army provisions."
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to propose: "The rich land north and south of the Bian embankment lies largely unused; it should be put under garrison farming to feed the troops."

sentences.zh: 乃分兵列營，以時種藝，選千夫長督勸之，事成，期年皆獲其利。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divided troops to set up camps, planted and cultivated in season, selected thousand-commanders to supervise and urge them on; when the work was done, within a year all reaped profit.
translations.idiomatic: He then divided his men into camps, sowed and harvested on schedule, and chose thousand-commanders to oversee the work. Within a year every unit had turned a profit.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，改懷遠大將軍、淄萊路緫管，尋兼軍事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he was changed to Grand General of Cherished Remoteness and intendant of the Zilai Circuit, and soon also held military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1271 he was made Grand General of Cherished Remoteness and intendant of the Zilai circuit, and soon afterward was given concurrent charge of military affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔伐宋，晉亨在選中，聞命就道，曰：「此報效之秋也。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict ordered the campaign against Song; Jinheng was among those selected; hearing the order he set out on the road and said: "This is the season to repay one's debt of service."
translations.idiomatic: In 1274, when an edict called for war on the Song, Jinheng was chosen for the campaign. As soon as he received the order he took the road, saying, "This is the moment to repay what I owe."

sentences.zh: 分道由安慶渡江，丞相伯顏留之戍鎮江，兼與民政，壹以鎮靜為務，戰焦山、瓜洲，皆有功。

translations.literal: Taking a separate route he crossed the Yangzi from Anqing; Chancellor Bayan kept him to garrison Zhenjiang and concurrently handle civil administration, making calm and stability his sole task; in battles at Jiaoshan and Guazhou he had merit both times.
translations.idiomatic: Marching by a separate route he crossed the Yangzi from Anqing. Chancellor Bayan left him to garrison Zhenjiang and also to oversee civil affairs, with keeping the region settled as his sole aim. He distinguished himself in the fighting at Jiaoshan and Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 子好古。

translations.literal: His son was Haogu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Haogu.

sentences.zh: 王珍字國寶，大名南樂人，世為農家，珍慷慨有大志。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen, courtesy name Guobao, was a man of Nanle in Daming; his family for generations were farmers; Zhen was generous and had great resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, whose courtesy name was Guobao, came from Nanle in Daming. His family had farmed for generations, but Zhen himself was openhanded and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 金末喪亂，所在盜起，南樂人楊鐵槍，聚衆保鄉里。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin there was turmoil and ruin; bandits rose everywhere; Yang Tieqiang of Nanle gathered a crowd to protect the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin dynasty collapsed into chaos, bandits sprang up everywhere. Yang Tieqiang of Nanle gathered men to defend the local countryside.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣兵攻破河朔，鐵槍以兵應之，行營帥按只署珍軍前都彈壓。

translations.literal: Taizu sent troops to break through Heshuo; Tieqiang responded with his forces; the field-camp commander Anzhi appointed Zhen as front-army chief suppressor.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu sent forces to overrun Heshuo, Tieqiang brought his troops over to meet them. The field commander Anzhi appointed Zhen chief suppressor of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 鐵槍與金軍戰死，衆推蘇椿代領其衆。

translations.literal: Tieqiang died fighting the Jin army; the multitude pushed Su Chun to take his place in leading the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Tieqiang was killed fighting the Jin army, and the men chose Su Chun to succeed him in command.

sentences.zh: 宋將彭義斌帥師侵大名，椿戰不利，降之，義斌遂據大名。

translations.literal: The Song general Peng Yibin led troops to invade Daming; Chun fought poorly and surrendered to him; Yibin thereupon occupied Daming.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commander Peng Yibin marched on Daming. Chun was defeated and submitted; Yibin then held the city.

sentences.zh: 珍棄其家，間道走還軍中，按只嘉其誠，待遇益厚，以為假子。

translations.literal: Zhen abandoned his household, took a by-path and fled back to the army; Anzhi praised his sincerity, treated him all the more generously, and made him a foster son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen left his family behind, stole back to the Mongol camp by a hidden route, and Anzhi, admiring his loyalty, treated him with still greater favor and took him as a foster son.

sentences.zh: 復從速魯忽擊走義斌，蘇椿以大名降，珍妻子故在，珍語之曰：「吾非棄汝輩，誠不以私愛奪吾報國之心耳。」

translations.literal: Again he followed Suluqu in driving off Yibin; Su Chun surrendered Daming; Zhen's wife and children were still there; Zhen said to them: "It is not that I abandoned you; truly I would not let private affection take away my heart to repay the state."
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Suluqu in driving Peng Yibin off, and Su Chun surrendered Daming. Zhen's wife and children were still in the city. He told them, "I did not cast you aside out of indifference—I simply would not let private love displace my duty to the state."

sentences.zh: 聞者稱歎。

translations.literal: Those who heard praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it spoke of him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 授鎮國上將軍、大名路治中、軍前行元帥府事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General Who Stabilizes the State, judicial commissioner of the Daming Circuit, and handler of the Forward Campaign Marshalate's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand General Who Stabilizes the State, judicial commissioner on the Daming circuit, and administrator of the forward campaign marshalate.

sentences.zh: 俄以取寧海、胙城功，遷輔國上將軍，復授統攝開曹滑濬等處行元帥府事，兼大名路安撫使。

translations.literal: Soon for merit in taking Ninghai and Zuocheng he was transferred to Grand General Who Assists the State, and again appointed to oversee the Forward Marshalate of Kai, Cao, Hua, Jun, and other places, concurrently serving as pacification commissioner of the Daming Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, for capturing Ninghai and Zuocheng, he was promoted to Grand General Who Assists the State and given overall charge of the forward marshalate for Kai, Cao, Hua, Jun, and neighboring districts, while also serving as pacification commissioner of Daming.

sentences.zh: 蘇椿復欲叛歸金，珍覺之，與元帥梁仲先發兵攻椿，椿開南門而遁。

translations.literal: Su Chun again wished to rebel and return to Jin; Zhen detected it; with Marshal Liang Zhongxian he raised troops to attack Chun; Chun opened the south gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Chun prepared to rebel and rejoin the Jin, Zhen discovered the plot. He and Marshal Liang Zhongxian marched against him, and Chun slipped out through the south gate and escaped.

sentences.zh: 國王斡真授仲行省，珍驃騎衛上將軍、同知大名府事、兼兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: Prince Wozhen appointed Zhong to a Branch Secretariat; Zhen was made Grand General of the Swift-Cavalry Guard, associate prefect of Daming Prefecture, and concurrently overall marshal of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wozhen made Zhong head of a branch secretariat and appointed Zhen Grand General of the Swift-Cavalry Guard, associate prefect of Daming, and overall marshal of cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 從速不台經略河南，破金將武仙于鄭州，復與金人戰于蕭縣，斬其將。

translations.literal: Following Subetei in pacifying Henan, he defeated the Jin general Wu Xian at Zhengzhou; again he fought Jin men at Xiao County and beheaded their general.
translations.idiomatic: Under Subetei's pacification of Henan he routed the Jin commander Wu Xian at Zhengzhou, and in a later battle at Xiao County he killed another Jin general.

sentences.zh: 頃之，仲死，國王命仲妻冉守真權行省事，珍為大名路尚書省下都元帥，將其軍。

translations.literal: Before long Zhong died; the Prince ordered Zhong's wife Ran Shouzhen to hold Branch Secretariat affairs provisionally; Zhen became Branch Secretariat deputy marshal under the Daming Circuit's Ministry of Revenue and led his army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhong died. The prince put Zhong's widow Ran Shouzhen in provisional charge of the branch secretariat and made Zhen deputy marshal under the Daming secretariat, commanding Zhong's troops.

sentences.zh: 國用安據徐、邳，珍從太赤及阿朮魯攻拔之，授同僉大名行省事。

translations.literal: Guo Yong'an held Xu and Pi; Zhen followed Taichi and Ajuru in attacking and taking them; he was appointed associate commissioner of the Daming Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong'an held Xu and Pi. Zhen followed Taichi and Ajuru in storming and taking them, and was appointed associate commissioner of the Daming branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從軍伐宋，破光州、棗陽、廬、壽、滁州，珍常身先諸將，屢有功。

translations.literal: Following the army in campaigning against Song, he broke Guangzhou, Zaoyang, Lu, Shou, and Chuzhou; Zhen often went before the generals in person and repeatedly had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaigns against the Song he helped capture Guang, Zaoyang, Lu, Shou, and Chu. Zhen repeatedly led from the front and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 宋城五河口，珍帥死士二十人奪之，宋人遁，乘勝進師，連破濠、泗、渦口。

translations.literal: Song fortified Wuhekou; Zhen led twenty death-defying men to seize it; Song men fled; riding victory he advanced the army and in succession broke Hao, Si, and Wokou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song fortified Wukou, Zhen led twenty picked men in a daring assault and took it. The Song forces fled, and he pressed the advantage, capturing Hao, Si, and Wokou in succession.

sentences.zh: 歲庚子，入見太宗，授緫帥本路軍馬管民次官，佩金符。

translations.literal: In the year gengzi he entered audience with Taizong and was appointed deputy to the commander-in-chief over this circuit's troops, horses, and civil population, wearing a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In 1240 he had an audience with Taizong and was made deputy to the circuit commander-in-chief over troops, horses, and the civilian population, with a gold tally of authority.

sentences.zh: 珍言於帝曰：「大名困於賦調，貸借西域賈人銀八十鋌，及逋糧五萬斛，若復征之，民無生者矣。」

translations.literal: Zhen said to the Emperor: "Daming is distressed by tax levies; it has borrowed eighty ingots of silver from Western Region merchants and owes fifty thousand hu of grain; if these are levied again, the people will have nothing left to live on."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen told the emperor, "Daming is crushed by levies. The circuit has borrowed eighty ingots of silver from Western merchants and still owes fifty thousand hu of grain in arrears. If we collect again, the people will have nothing left to live on."

sentences.zh: 詔官償所借銀，復盡蠲其逋糧。

translations.literal: An edict ordered officials to repay the borrowed silver and again completely remitted the grain in arrears.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the government to repay the borrowed silver and remitted the entire grain debt.

sentences.zh: 已而朝廷議分蒙古、漢軍戍河南，以珍戍睢州，修城隍，明斥候，宋兵不敢犯。

translations.literal: Before long the court discussed dividing Mongol and Han armies to garrison Henan; Zhen was assigned to garrison Suizhou; he repaired walls and moats and made scouts clear; Song troops did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when the court decided to divide Mongol and Han troops to garrison Henan, Zhen was posted to Suizhou. He repaired the walls and ditches and kept scouts alert, and Song forces did not dare approach.

sentences.zh: 己酉，入朝定宗，進本路征行萬戶，加金虎符。

translations.literal: In jiyou he entered court to Dingzong and was advanced to campaign ten-thousand-household of this circuit, with a gold tiger tally added.
translations.idiomatic: In 1249 he attended Dingzong at court, was promoted to campaign ten-thousand-household of his circuit, and received a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 在鎮九年，卒，年六十五。

translations.literal: Garrisoning nine years, he died, age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years in command he died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子文幹，善騎射，襲為行軍萬戶。

translations.literal: His son Wengan was skilled in mounted archery and inherited the post as campaign ten-thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wengan, an expert horseman and archer, inherited his father's post as campaign ten-thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 己未，從世祖攻鄂州，先登，中流矢，賜以良馬、金帛。

translations.literal: In jiwei he followed Shizu in attacking Ezhou, was first to ascend, was struck by a flying arrow, and was granted a fine horse and gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1259 he followed Kublai in the assault on Ezhou, was the first man up the wall, took an arrow in the fight, and was rewarded with a fine horse, gold, and silks.

sentences.zh: 李璮叛，從哈必赤討平之，哈必赤論功，語以官賞，文幹對曰：「增秩則榮及一身，賜金則恩逮麾下。」

translations.literal: When Li Tan rebelled he followed Habichi in suppressing and pacifying him; Habichi assessed merit and spoke of office and reward; Wengan replied: "If rank is raised, glory reaches one man alone; if gold is granted, favor reaches those under command."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tan rebelled, he followed Habichi in putting down the revolt. Habichi offered him rank or reward for his service. Wengan replied, "A promotion would honor only me, but gold could reach the men under my command."

sentences.zh: 迺以白金二千兩、器皿百事、雜綵數百縑賞之，文幹悉頒之軍中。

translations.literal: Thereupon two thousand taels of white gold, a hundred pieces of vessels, and several hundred bolts of miscellaneous silks were granted him; Wengan distributed them all in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore given two thousand taels of silver, a hundred pieces of tableware, and several hundred bolts of assorted silks, all of which Wengan distributed among his troops.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，制：「父兄弟子並仕同塗者，罷其弟子。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong a regulation stated: "Where father, elder brother, and son all serve on the same track, the younger brother or son is to be dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 a statute provided: "When father, elder brother, and son all hold office in the same branch of service, the younger brother or son must resign."

sentences.zh: 文幹弟文禮為千戶，文幹自陳，願解己官而留文禮，詔從之。

translations.literal: Wengan's younger brother Wenli was a thousand-household; Wengan submitted himself, wishing to relinquish his own office and keep Wenli; an edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Wengan's younger brother Wenli was a thousand-household. Wengan petitioned to resign his own post so that Wenli could remain, and the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 改同知大名路緫管府事，累遷河東山西道提刑按察副使。

translations.literal: He was changed to associate intendant of the Daming Circuit Directorate; he was repeatedly transferred to vice surveillance commissioner of the Hedong and Shanxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as associate intendant of the Daming circuit directorate and eventually rose to vice surveillance commissioner on the Hedong-Shanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 近臣言其鄂州之功，陞僉東川行樞密院事，歷全州、衛輝、東平緫管，改江東建康道提刑按察使，卒于官，年五十八。

translations.literal: A close minister spoke of his Ezhou merit; he was advanced to commissioner of the Eastern Chuan Branch Privy Council; he passed through posts as intendant of Quanzhou, Weihui, and Dongping; was changed to surveillance commissioner of the Jiangdong Jiankang Circuit; died in office, age fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: When a court favorite cited his service at Ezhou, he was promoted to commissioner of the Eastern Sichuan branch privy council, then served successively as intendant of Quan, Weihui, and Dongping, and finally as surveillance commissioner on the Jiangdong-Jiankang circuit. He died in office at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 發其篋中，錢僅七緡，貧不能歸葬，人以此稱之。

translations.literal: Opening his document case, money was only seven strings; he was too poor to return for burial; people for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When his effects were opened, they found only seven strings of cash—too little even to send his body home for burial. People spoke of him with respect for that very reason.

sentences.zh: 楊傑只哥

translations.literal: Yang Jiezhige.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiezhige

sentences.zh: 楊傑只哥，燕京寶坻人，家世業農。

translations.literal: Yang Jiezhige was a man of Baodi in Yanjing; his family for generations practiced farming.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiezhige came from Baodi in the Yan capital region. His family had been farmers for generations.

sentences.zh: 傑只哥少有勇略，太祖略地燕、趙，率族屬降附。

translations.literal: Jiezhige in youth had courage and stratagem; when Taizu overran the lands of Yan and Zhao, he led his clan and dependents to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man Jiezhige showed courage and tactical sense. When Taizu overran Yan and Zhao, he led his kinsmen in submission.

sentences.zh: 從攻遼左，及從元帥阿朮魯定西夏諸部，有功。

translations.literal: He followed in attacking eastern Liao, and followed Marshal Ajuru in settling the various parts of Western Xia, with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in eastern Liao and followed Marshal Ajuru in subduing the Western Xia tribes, earning distinction in both.

sentences.zh: 己丑，睿宗賜以金幣，命從阿朮魯攻信安，阿朮魯知其材略出諸將右，命裁決軍務。

translations.literal: In jichou Ruizong granted him gold and coins and ordered him to follow Ajuru in attacking Xin'an; Ajuru knew his talent and plans surpassed the generals on the right and ordered him to decide military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1229 Ruizong rewarded him with gold and coin and ordered him to follow Ajuru against Xin'an. Ajuru, seeing that his talent outshone the other commanders, put him in charge of military decisions.

sentences.zh: 信安城四面阻水，其帥張進數月不降，傑只哥曰：「彼恃巨浸，我師進不得利，退不得歸，不若往說之。」

translations.literal: Xin'an city's four sides were blocked by water; its commander Zhang Jin for several months would not surrender; Jiezhige said: "They rely on vast floods; our army advancing cannot gain advantage, retreating cannot return—better to go and persuade them."
translations.idiomatic: Xin'an was moated on every side, and its commander Zhang Jin had refused surrender for months. Jiezhige said, "They trust the wide waters around them. We cannot advance with profit or retreat in safety. Better to go and persuade them."

sentences.zh: 進見其來，怒曰：「吾已斬二使，汝不懼死耶？」

translations.literal: Jin saw him come and angrily said: "I have already beheaded two envoys—are you not afraid of death?"
translations.idiomatic: When Jin saw him arrive, he raged, "I have already executed two envoys. Are you not afraid to die?"

sentences.zh: 傑只哥無懼色，從容言曰：「今齊、魯、燕、趙，地方數千里，郡邑聞風納降，獨君恃此一城，內無軍儲，外無兵援，亡可立待。

translations.literal: Jiezhige had no look of fear and calmly said: "Now Qi, Lu, Yan, and Zhao—territory of several thousand li—prefectures and districts hear the wind and submit; you alone rely on this one city; within there are no army stores, without there is no military aid; destruction can be awaited standing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhige showed no fear and answered calmly, "For a thousand li across Qi, Lu, Yan, and Zhao, districts have been surrendering at the first rumor of our approach. You alone cling to this one town with no stores within and no relief without. Your fall can come at any moment.

sentences.zh: 為君計者，不如請降，可以保富貴而免死亡。」

translations.literal: For your planning, sir, it would be better to request surrender—you can preserve wealth and honor and avoid death."
translations.idiomatic: If you take counsel for yourself, you would do better to submit and keep your wealth and rank while escaping death."

sentences.zh: 進默然曰：「姑待之。」

translations.literal: Jin was silent and said: "For the moment wait."
translations.idiomatic: Jin was silent, then said, "Wait awhile."

sentences.zh: 凡三往，乃降。

translations.literal: In all he went three times; then they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhige went three times in all before Jin finally surrendered.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，大名守蘇椿叛，討獲之，衆議屠城，傑只哥曰：「怒一人而族萬家，非招來之道也。」

translations.literal: In xinmao the Daming defender Su Chun rebelled; pursued and captured, the multitude discussed slaughtering the city; Jiezhige said: "In anger at one man to exterminate ten thousand households is not the way to win people over."
translations.idiomatic: In 1231 Su Chun, the defender of Daming, rebelled and was captured after a punitive campaign. Some urged that the city be put to the sword. Jiezhige said, "To punish one man by destroying ten thousand households is no way to win people over."

sentences.zh: 衆是其言。

translations.literal: The multitude approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 由是滑、濬等州，聞風納款。

translations.literal: From this Hua, Jun, and other prefectures heard the wind and submitted pledges.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Hua, Jun, and neighboring prefectures submitted at the first news of the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，師次徐州，阻河不得濟。

translations.literal: In renchen the army halted at Xuzhou; blocked by the river they could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: In 1232 the army reached Xuzhou but was stopped by the river and could not cross.

sentences.zh: 傑只哥探知有賊兵操舟楫伏草澤中，率勁卒數人，憑河擊之，悉奪舟楫，衆遂得渡，獲河南諸郡降人三萬餘戶。

translations.literal: Jiezhige reconnoitered and learned there were bandit troops handling boats and ships hidden in grass and marshes; he led several crack soldiers, leaning on the river struck them, seized all boats and ships entirely; the multitude then could cross and obtained more than thirty thousand surrendered households of Henan's various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jiezhige discovered enemy skirmishers with boats hidden in the reed marshes. He took a few picked men, attacked along the riverbank, and seized every boat. The army crossed, taking more than thirty thousand surrendered households from the Henan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 進攻徐州，金將國用安拒戰，傑只哥率百餘騎突入陣中，迎擊於後，大敗之，擒一將而還。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Xuzhou, the Jin general Guo Yong'an resisted battle; Jiezhige led a hundred-odd horsemen to burst into the formation, met and struck from the rear, greatly defeated them, seized one general and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Xuzhou the Jin commander Guo Yong'an gave battle. Jiezhige led a little more than a hundred horsemen in a charge through the enemy line, then wheeled and struck from the rear, routing them and bringing back a captured general.

sentences.zh: 皇太弟國王駐兵河上，見之，賜名拔都，授金符，命緫管新附軍民。

translations.literal: The Imperial Younger Brother Prince encamped troops on the river; seeing him, he bestowed the name Batu, granted a gold tally, and ordered him to oversee newly submitted troops and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial prince, campaigning on the river, saw his deed and gave him the name Batu, a gold tally, and command over the newly submitted troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 乙未，太宗特賜傑只哥種田民戶租賦。

translations.literal: In yiwei Taizong specially granted Jiezhige the tax levies of farming civilian households.
translations.idiomatic: In 1235 Taizong specially granted Jiezhige the tax income of the farming households under his charge.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，從阿朮魯攻歸德，傑只哥麾諸將縛草作筏渡濠抵城下，梯城先登，拔之。

translations.literal: In dingyou he followed Ajuru in attacking Guide; Jiezhige directed the generals to bind grass to make rafts, cross the moat and reach below the wall, ladder the wall and ascend first, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1237 he followed Ajuru against Guide. Jiezhige had his officers bind straw into rafts, cross the moat, reach the wall, and scale it—he himself was first up and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 由是進攻，得五州十縣四堡二寨。

translations.literal: From this in advancing attacks he obtained five prefectures, ten counties, four forts, and two stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the continuing campaign he took five prefectures, ten counties, four forts, and two stockades.

sentences.zh: 己亥，宋兵至，已登歸德城，傑只哥率衆拒戰，敗之。

translations.literal: In jihai Song troops arrived and had already ascended Guide's walls; Jiezhige led the multitude to resist battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1239 Song forces arrived and had already gained the walls of Guide. Jiezhige led his men in a counterattack and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 率舟師追擊，轉戰中流，溺死，年四十。

translations.literal: Leading boat forces in pursuit, turning battle in mid-stream, he drowned and died, age forty.
translations.idiomatic: Leading a naval pursuit, he was caught in midstream fighting and drowned. He was forty.

sentences.zh: 子孝先、孝友。

translations.literal: His sons were Xiaoxian and Xiaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xiaoxian and Xiaoyou.

sentences.zh: 孝先，僉江北淮東道肅政廉訪司事。

translations.literal: Xiaoxian was commissioner of the Jiangbei Huai-East Circuit's Office for Imperial Government and Honest Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxian served as commissioner of the Jiangbei-Huai-East circuit's surveillance office for honest administration.

sentences.zh: 孝友，鎮江路緫管。

translations.literal: Xiaoyou was intendant of the Zhenjiang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyou was intendant of the Zhenjiang circuit.

sentences.zh: 劉通字仲達，東平齊河人也。

translations.literal: Liu Tong, courtesy name Zhongda, was a man of Qihe in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tong, whose courtesy name was Zhongda, came from Qihe in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 初從嚴實來歸，繼從收濮、曹、相、潞、定陶、楚丘。

translations.literal: At first he followed Yan Shi in coming to submit; afterward he followed in taking Pu, Cao, Xiang, Lu, Dingtao, and Chuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Yan Shi in submission, then took part in the capture of Pu, Cao, Xiang, Lu, Dingtao, and Chuqiu.

sentences.zh: 實薦于太師木華黎，以通為齊河緫管，尋授鎮國上將軍、左副都元帥、濟南知府、德州緫管、行軍千戶。

translations.literal: Shi recommended him to Grand Preceptor Muqali; Tong was made intendant of Qihe; soon he was appointed Grand General Who Stabilizes the State, left vice overall marshal, prefect of Jinan, intendant of Dezhou, and campaign thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: Shi recommended him to Grand Preceptor Muqali, who made him intendant of Qihe and soon afterward appointed him Grand General Who Stabilizes the State, left vice marshal, prefect of Jinan, intendant of Dezhou, and campaign thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 太宗錫金符，陞上千戶。

translations.literal: Taizong granted a gold tally and raised him to thousand-household.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong gave him a gold tally and promoted him to thousand-household.

sentences.zh: 宋將彭義斌攻齊河城，率衆夜登，通與六七人鼓譟而進，宋人驚懼，墜溺死者甚衆。

translations.literal: The Song general Peng Yibin attacked Qihe city, led a crowd to ascend by night; Tong with six or seven men beat drums and clamored as they advanced; Song men were startled and afraid; many fell and drowned in death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song commander Peng Yibin assaulted Qihe by night and led his men onto the walls, Tong advanced with only six or seven companions, beating drums and shouting. The Song troops panicked, and many fell from the walls and drowned.

sentences.zh: 明日復合，圍城三匝，通令守陴者植槊如櫛，俄從撤去，宋人懼其向己也，大潰，義斌僅以數騎免。

translations.literal: The next day they joined battle again and surrounded the city three circuits deep; Tong ordered the wall defenders to plant spears like a comb; soon they withdrew from following; Song men feared they were turning on them and fled in great rout; Yibin escaped with only several horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the enemy returned and ringed the city three deep. Tong had the defenders plant spears along the battlements like a hedge, then suddenly pull them back. The Song army, fearing a sally, broke in full rout, and Yibin escaped with only a handful of horsemen.

sentences.zh: 歲丁酉，遷德州等處二萬戶軍民緫管。

translations.literal: In the year dingyou he was transferred to overall commander of the two-ten-thousand-household troops and civilians of Dezhou and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In 1237 he was made overall commander of the two-ten-thousand-household forces and civilian population of Dezhou and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 歲丙辰卒。

translations.literal: In the year bingchen he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1256.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，進左翼侍衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan he was advanced to commander of the Left Wing Palace Guard's personal army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1265 he was promoted to commander of the Left Wing Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷右翼。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to the Right Wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to the Right Wing.

sentences.zh: 九年，加昭勇大將軍、鳳州等處經略使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was given Grand General of Manifest Courage and pacification commissioner of Fengzhou and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Grand General of Manifest Courage and pacification commissioner of Fengzhou and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷征東左副都元帥，統軍四萬、戰船九百，征日本，與倭兵十萬遇，戰敗之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to left vice overall marshal for the Eastern Campaign, commanding forty thousand troops and nine hundred war boats to campaign against Japan; he met one hundred thousand Wa troops and in battle defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was made left vice marshal for the eastern campaign, commanding forty thousand men and nine hundred warships against Japan. He met a Japanese force of one hundred thousand and defeated it in battle.

sentences.zh: 還，招降淮南諸郡邑。

translations.literal: Returning, he summoned surrender of Huainan's various prefectures and districts.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he received the submission of prefectures and districts throughout Huainan.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授昭信路緫管。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed intendant of the Zhaoxin Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was appointed intendant of the Zhaoxin circuit.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷黃州宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to pacification commissioner of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made pacification commissioner of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，改太平路緫管，俄授鎮國上將軍，為淮西道宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was changed to intendant of the Taiping Circuit; soon he was appointed Grand General Who Stabilizes the State and served as overall marshal and pacification commissioner of the Huaixi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was reassigned as intendant of the Taiping circuit and soon made Grand General Who Stabilizes the State and overall pacification marshal of the Huaixi circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加奉國上將軍。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was given Grand General Who Serves the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Grand General Who Serves the State.

sentences.zh: 三月，卒。

translations.literal: In the third month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month.

sentences.zh: 子五人：浩，澤，澧，淵，淮。

translations.literal: He had five sons: Hao, Ze, Li, Yuan, and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Hao, Ze, Li, Yuan, and Huai.

sentences.zh: 浩，中統四年襲千戶，至元八年歿于兵。

translations.literal: Hao inherited the thousand-household post in the fourth year of Zhongtong and died in battle in the eighth year of Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hao inherited the thousand-household rank in 1263 and fell in battle in 1271.

sentences.zh: 澤，由近侍出為荊湖北道宣慰使。

translations.literal: Ze left palace service to become pacification commissioner of the Jingbei-Huai Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Ze left the inner court to serve as pacification commissioner on the Jingbei-Huai circuit.

sentences.zh: 澧，知長寧州。

translations.literal: Li was magistrate of Changning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li served as magistrate of Changning.

sentences.zh: 俱蚤卒。

translations.literal: All died young.
translations.idiomatic: All three died young.

sentences.zh: 淵，至元十一年，佩金符，授進義副尉，為徐、邳屯田緫管下丁莊千戶。

translations.literal: Yuan, in the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, wore a gold tally and was appointed Deputy Vice Commissioner of Manifest Righteousness, serving as Dingzhuang thousand-household under the Xu-Pi garrison farming commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 Yuan received a gold tally and was made Deputy Vice Commissioner of Manifest Righteousness, with a post as Dingzhuang thousand-household under the Xu-Pi garrison farming command.

sentences.zh: 九月，領兵巡邏泗州，至淮河九里灣，遇宋軍，戰勝，奪其船三十餘艘。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he led troops patrolling Sizhou; reaching Jiuli Bay on the Huai River he met Song troops, defeated them, and seized more than thirty of their boats.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he patrolled Sizhou, and at Jiuli Bay on the Huai he met Song forces, defeated them, and captured more than thirty boats.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，與宋安撫朱煥戰于清河，敗之，擒十四人，奪其輜重。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year he fought Song pacification commissioner Zhu Huan at Qinghe, defeated him, captured fourteen men, and seized his baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1275 he fought the Song pacification commissioner Zhu Huan at Qinghe, routed him, took fourteen prisoners, and seized his supply train.

sentences.zh: 九月，從右丞別乞里迷失攻淮安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he followed Right Chancellor Beg Irin Qusu in attacking Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he followed the right chancellor Beg Irin Qusu against Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 十三年，與宋人戰昭信軍南靖平山。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he fought Song troops at Ping Mountain south of Nanjing in Zhaoxin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 he fought Song forces at Ping Mountain south of Nanjing in Zhaoxin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俱有功。

translations.literal: In each he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: In each engagement he won distinction.

sentences.zh: 十四年，北覲，進武略將軍、管軍緫管。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he had a northern audience and was advanced to General of Martial Strategy and overall troop commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 he attended court in the north and was promoted to General of Martial Strategy and overall commander of troops.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從元帥張弘範征閩、廣、漳、韶諸州，以功授武德將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Marshal Zhang Hongfan in campaigning in Fujian, Guang, Zhang, and Shao, and for merit was appointed General of Martial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he followed Marshal Zhang Hongfan against Fujian, Guang, Zhang, and Shao and was made General of Martial Virtue for his service.

sentences.zh: 十六年，從攻崖山，弘範命淵領後翼軍，水戰有功。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he followed the attack on Yamen; Hongfan ordered Yuan to lead the rear-wing army and he had merit in naval fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In 1279, in the assault on Yamen, Hongfan put Yuan in command of the rear wing, where he distinguished himself in the naval battle.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進安遠大將軍，為副招討。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was advanced to Grand General of Pacifying the Distant and made deputy pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1280 he was promoted to Grand General of Pacifying the Distant and appointed deputy pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，遷潁州副萬戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to vice ten-thousand-household of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 he was made vice ten-thousand-household of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，從征交趾，鎮南王脫歡命領水步軍二萬，攻萬劫江，擒十六人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he followed the campaign against Annam; Prince of Pacifying the South Toqto ordered him to lead twenty thousand naval and infantry troops, attacked Wanjie River, and captured sixteen men.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 he joined the campaign against Annam. The Prince of Pacifying the South, Toqto, put him in charge of twenty thousand land and naval troops; at Wanjie River he took sixteen prisoners.

sentences.zh: 繼攻靈山城，賊衆迎敵，大敗之，師還。

translations.literal: Continuing to attack Lingshan city, the rebel host came out to meet him; he greatly defeated them and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then attacked Lingshan, routed the rebels who came out to meet him, and withdrew with the army.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，捕寇浙東，獲其酋長三人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he hunted bandits in eastern Zhejiang and captured three of their chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 he suppressed bandits in eastern Zhejiang and captured three chieftains.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，兼領紹興浙江五翼軍，守杭州，繼以疾卒，大德十一年卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he concurrently commanded the five wings of the Shaoxing-Zhejiang army, garrisoned Hangzhou, and later died of illness; he died in the eleventh year of Dade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1294 he also took command of the five wings of the Shaoxing-Zhejiang army and garrisoned Hangzhou; he later died of illness, in 1307.

sentences.zh: 子無晦，至大元年，襲授昭信校尉、潁州副萬戶，俄進武德將軍。

translations.literal: His son Wuhui, in the first year of Zhida, inherited appointment as Commandant of Manifest Trust and vice ten-thousand-household of Yingzhou, and soon was advanced to General of Martial Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wuhui, in 1308, inherited the posts of Commandant of Manifest Trust and vice ten-thousand-household of Yingzhou and was soon promoted to General of Martial Virtue.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年，以病免。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou he was dismissed because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1318 he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 六年，改河南江北行省都鎮撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed to overall pacification commissioner of the Henan-Jiangbei Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the following year he was made overall pacification commissioner of the Henan-Jiangbei branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，加宣武將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he was given General of Manifest Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: In 1327 he was granted the rank of General of Manifest Martiality.

sentences.zh: 岳存字彥誠，大名冠氏人。

translations.literal: Yue Cun, courtesy name Yancheng, was a man of Guanshi in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Cun, whose courtesy name was Yancheng, came from Guanshi in Daming.

sentences.zh: 初歸東平嚴實，承制授存武德將軍、帥府都緫領，保冠氏。

translations.literal: At first he submitted to Yan Shi of Dongping; acting by order he was appointed General of Martial Virtue and overall leader of the marshalate, protecting Guanshi.
translations.idiomatic: He first submitted to Yan Shi of Dongping and, by provisional appointment, was made General of Martial Virtue and overall leader of the marshalate, charged with defending Guanshi.

sentences.zh: 會金從宜鄭倜復據大名，距冠氏僅三十里，遣兵來攻。

translations.literal: It happened that the Jin follower Zheng Tong again held Daming, only thirty li from Guanshi, and sent troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin loyalist Zheng Tong again seized Daming, only thirty li from Guanshi, he sent troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 倜不得志，復自將萬人合圍，其勢甚張。

translations.literal: Tong did not achieve his aim and again personally led ten thousand men in a combined siege; their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Tong failed to prevail and returned at the head of ten thousand men to invest the town; their force was formidable.

sentences.zh: 存率死士百餘，突出西門，勇氣十倍。

translations.literal: Cun led a hundred-odd death-defying men and burst out the west gate; their courage was tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Cun led a little more than a hundred picked men in a sortie through the west gate, fighting with redoubled courage.

sentences.zh: 金人退走，存追之，越境乃還。

translations.literal: Jin men retreated and fled; Cun pursued them and returned only after crossing the border.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin troops broke and fled. Cun pursued them beyond the border before turning back.

sentences.zh: 歲己丑，從嚴實及武仙戰于彰德西，敗之，遷明威將軍，行冠氏主簿。

translations.literal: In the year jichou he followed Yan Shi and Wu Xian in battle west of Zhangde and defeated them; he was transferred to General of Manifest Authority and acting chief clerk of Guanshi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1229 he followed Yan Shi and Wu Xian to battle west of Zhangde, won, and was made General of Manifest Authority and acting chief clerk of Guanshi.

sentences.zh: 明年，存率騎兵二百、步卒三百，自彰德北還。

translations.literal: The next year Cun led two hundred cavalry and three hundred infantry returning north from Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he led two hundred horsemen and three hundred foot soldiers north from Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 至開州南，與金將張開遇，開衆萬餘，存軍依大林，戒其軍曰：「彼衆我寡，不可輕動，當聽吾鼓聲為節。」

translations.literal: South of Kaizhou he met the Jin general Zhang Kai; Kai's host was more than ten thousand; Cun's army relied on a great forest; he warned his troops: "They are many, we few; do not move lightly—you must heed my drumbeats as the signal."
translations.idiomatic: South of Kaizhou he encountered the Jin commander Zhang Kai with more than ten thousand men. Cun drew up his force in a great wood and warned his men, "They outnumber us; do not stir until you hear my drum."

sentences.zh: 乃命騎士居前，步卒次之，與敵相去僅二十步，一鼓作氣，無不一當百，開衆大潰，追二十餘里，不損一卒而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered horsemen in front and foot soldiers behind; they were only twenty paces from the enemy; at one drumbeat all were as ten; Kai's host fled in great rout; they pursued more than twenty li and returned without losing a single soldier.
translations.idiomatic: He put the cavalry forward and the infantry behind. When they were only twenty paces from the enemy, a single drumroll sent every man fighting as ten. Zhang Kai's army collapsed; Cun pursued more than twenty li and returned without losing a man.

sentences.zh: 破河南，攻淮、漢，無役不與。

translations.literal: Breaking Henan, attacking Huai and Han—there was no campaign in which he did not take part.
translations.idiomatic: From the conquest of Henan to campaigns on the Huai and Han, he took part in every fight.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，陞本縣丞。

translations.literal: In xinchou he was promoted to assistant magistrate of his county.
translations.idiomatic: In 1241 he was promoted to assistant magistrate of his home county.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，移治楚丘，數年，有惠政。

translations.literal: In gengxu he moved administration to Chuqiu; after several years he had benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: In 1250 he was transferred to administer Chuqiu, where after several years his rule won the people's affection.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，告老退休田里。

translations.literal: In yimao he reported old age and retired to his village fields.
translations.idiomatic: In 1255 he pleaded age and retired to his home village.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，以疾卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he died of illness, age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In 1262 he died of illness at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子天禎，襲父職冠氏縣軍民彈壓，從圍襄樊，帥府承制授管軍百戶，修立百丈山、鹿門等堡。

translations.literal: His son Tianzhen inherited his father's post as military suppressor of Guanshi County's troops and civilians; following the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng, the marshalate by provisional order appointed him commander of a hundred troops; he built the forts of Baizhang Mountain, Lumen, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianzhen inherited his father's post as military suppressor over the troops and civilians of Guanshi. During the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng the marshalate provisionally made him commander of a hundred troops, and he built the forts at Baizhang Mountain, Lumen, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 天禎率銳士，冒矢石，從樊城東北先登，為木所傷，墮地，復躡梯以登，手刃數人。

translations.literal: Tianzhen led crack troops, braved arrows and stones, and from the northeast of Fancheng was first to ascend; he was struck by timber, fell to the ground, again trampled the ladder to ascend, and with his own hand killed several men.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhen led picked men through arrow and stone fire, was first up the northeast wall of Fancheng, was struck by a beam and fell, then climbed the ladder again and killed several defenders with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 築正陽東西城，及於鎮江造戰船，天禎咸董其役。

translations.literal: Building the eastern and western cities of Zhengyang and constructing war boats at Zhenjiang—Tianzhen supervised all these tasks.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw construction of the eastern and western cities at Zhengyang and the building of warships at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 戰焦山，平奉化賊，錄功陞管軍千戶。

translations.literal: Fighting at Jiaoshan and pacifying the Fenghua rebels, his recorded merit raised him to commander of a thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiaoshan and in pacifying the Fenghua rebels his merits won him promotion to commander of a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 江南平，從元帥張弘範覲帝于柳林，賜金錦、銀鞍勒。

translations.literal: When the south was pacified he followed Marshal Zhang Hongfan to audience with the Emperor at Liulin and was granted gold brocade and a silver saddle and bridle.
translations.idiomatic: After the south was pacified he followed Marshal Zhang Hongfan to audience at Liulin and received gold brocade and a silver saddle and bridle.

sentences.zh: 授昭勇大將軍、福州路緫管，平尤溪賊。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General of Manifest Courage and intendant of the Fuzhou Circuit, and pacified the Youxi bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand General of Manifest Courage and intendant of Fuzhou, where he pacified the Youxi bandits.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，改吉州，平永新賊，後遷贛州。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was changed to Jizhou, pacified the Yongxin bandits, and later was transferred to Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was sent to Jizhou, subdued the Yongxin bandits, and was later transferred to Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷建康，首定救荒之政，民立碑以紀遺愛焉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Jiankang, first established famine-relief policy, and the people erected a stele to record his lingering affection.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was moved to Jiankang, where he first instituted famine relief; the people raised a stele in memory of his kindness.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，卒于建康，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida he died at Jiankang, age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 he died at Jiankang at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子果，會昌州同知。

translations.literal: His son Guo was associate prefect of Huichang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guo served as associate prefect of Huichang.

sentences.zh: 張子良懋

translations.literal: Zhang Ziliang Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ziliang: Mao

sentences.zh: 張子良字漢臣，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ziliang, courtesy name Hanchen, was a man of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ziliang, whose courtesy name was Hanchen, came from Fanyang in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 金末四方兵起，所在募兵自保。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin armies rose everywhere and each place recruited troops to protect itself.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin dynasty collapsed, militias sprang up everywhere to defend local communities.

sentences.zh: 子良率千餘人入燕、薊間，耕稼已絕，遂聚州人，阻水，治舟筏，取蒲魚自給，從之者衆，至不能容。

translations.literal: Ziliang led a thousand-odd men into the Yan and Ji region; farming and harvesting had ceased, so he gathered the people of the prefecture, blocked the water, built rafts and boats, took cattails and fish to support themselves; those who followed were many, until they could not be contained.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang led more than a thousand men into the Yan and Ji region. With farming at a standstill, he gathered the local people, dammed the waterways, built rafts, and lived on reeds and fish. So many followed him that the settlement could hold no more.

sentences.zh: 子良部勒定興、新城數萬口，就食東平，東平守納之。

translations.literal: Ziliang organized and commanded several tens of thousands from Dingxing and Xincheng and went to Dongping for food; the Dongping defender admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He organized tens of thousands from Dingxing and Xincheng and moved them to Dongping for food; the local commander took them in.

sentences.zh: 久之，守棄東平還汴，檄子良南屯宿州，又南屯壽州。

translations.literal: Before long the defender abandoned Dongping and returned to Bian; he summoned Ziliang to garrison south at Suzhou, and again south at Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the commander abandoned Dongping for Bian and ordered Ziliang south to garrison Suzhou, then farther south at Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏全劫其民出雞口，李敏據州。

translations.literal: Xia Quan plundered his people out through Jikou; Li Min held the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Quan drove his people out through Jikou, while Li Min seized the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 子良率麾下造敏，敏欲害之，走歸宿，因以宿帥之衆奪全所劫老幼數萬以還。

translations.literal: Ziliang led his subordinates to visit Min; Min wished to harm him; he fled back to Su and thereby with the Su commander's troops seized the old and young numbering tens of thousands that Quan had plundered and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang went to Li Min with his men. Min meant to kill him, but he escaped back to Suzhou and, with the Suzhou commander's troops, recovered the tens of thousands of old and young Xia Quan had carried off.

sentences.zh: 全怒，連徐、邳之軍來攻。

translations.literal: Quan was enraged and linked the armies of Xu and Pi to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Quan in fury joined the forces of Xu and Pi in an attack.

sentences.zh: 子良與宿帥斫其營，全失其軍符，走死揚州。

translations.literal: Ziliang and the Suzhou commander cut down his camp; Quan lost his military tally and fled to die in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang and the Suzhou commander stormed his camp. Quan lost his military tally and fled to Yangzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 時金受重圍於汴，聲援盡絕，有國用安者，圖以漣水之衆入援，道阻，游兵不能進。

translations.literal: At that time Jin was under heavy siege at Bian; voices of support were entirely cut off; there was one Guo Yong'an who planned to lead the Lianshui troops to relieve them; the road was blocked and roaming soldiers could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was then tightly besieged at Bian with all relief cut off. Guo Yong'an planned to lead troops from Lianshui to the rescue, but the route was blocked and his scouts could not get through.

sentences.zh: 子良與一偏將，晝伏夜行，得入汴，達用安意。

translations.literal: Ziliang with one flank general, hiding by day and marching by night, was able to enter Bian and convey Yong'an's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang and a flank officer traveled by day in hiding and by night on the march, entered Bian, and delivered Yong'an's message.

sentences.zh: 金君臣以為自天降也，曲賜勞來，凡所欲，皆如用安請，因以徐、宿授子良。

translations.literal: Jin's ruler and ministers thought he had fallen from heaven; they graciously bestowed rewards; whatever was desired was as Yong'an requested; thereby Xu and Su were granted to Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court thought he had dropped from the sky. They honored him lavishly, granted Yong'an's every request, and gave Xu and Su to Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 明年，子良進米五百石于汴，授榮祿大夫，緫管陝西東路兵馬，仍治宿州。

translations.literal: The next year Ziliang presented five hundred shi of grain to Bian and was appointed Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and overall commander of Shaanxi East Route forces, still administering Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he sent five hundred shi of grain to Bian and was made Grand Master of Glorious Blessings and overall commander of the Shaanxi Eastern Route, while still governing Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 當是時，令已不行於陝，而用安亦卒不得志。

translations.literal: At that time orders already did not prevail in Shaanxi, and Yong'an also in the end could not achieve his aim.
translations.idiomatic: By then imperial orders no longer ran in Shaanxi, and Yong'an never achieved his purpose.

sentences.zh: 徐、宿之間，民無食者，出城拾穭穟以食，子良嚴兵護之，以防鈔掠。

translations.literal: Between Xu and Su the people had no food; they left the city to gather chaff and grain ears to eat; Ziliang strictly guarded them with troops to prevent plunder and raiding.
translations.idiomatic: Between Xu and Su the starving went outside the walls to gather chaff and fallen grain. Ziliang posted troops to protect them from looters.

sentences.zh: 猝遇敵。

translations.literal: Suddenly they met the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He suddenly encountered the enemy.

sentences.zh: 子良被重傷，乃率其衆就食泗州。

translations.literal: Ziliang was heavily wounded and thereupon led his multitude to seek food at Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Badly wounded, he led his people to Sizhou for food.

sentences.zh: 泗守閱兵，將圖之，子良與麾下十數人，即軍中生縛其守。

translations.literal: The Si defender reviewed troops and was about to plot against him; Ziliang with a dozen-odd of his subordinates bound the defender on the spot within the army.
translations.idiomatic: The Sizhou commander mustered troops intending to move against him. Ziliang and a dozen of his men seized and bound the commander in camp.

sentences.zh: 民不欲北歸者，欲走傍郡，子良資以舟楫，無敢掠其財物。

translations.literal: People who did not wish to return north wanted to flee to neighboring prefectures; Ziliang supplied them with boats and rafts, and none dared plunder their property.
translations.idiomatic: Those who did not wish to go north wanted to flee to neighboring prefectures; Ziliang gave them boats, and no one dared rob their goods.

sentences.zh: 歲戊戌，率泗州西城二十五縣、軍民十萬八千餘口，因元帥阿朮來歸。

translations.literal: In the year wuxu he led the twenty-five counties of Sizhou's western city and 108,000-odd troops and civilians and through Marshal Ajuru came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1238 he led the twenty-five counties of western Sizhou and more than 108,000 troops and civilians to submit through Marshal Ajuru.

sentences.zh: 太宗命為東路都緫帥，授銀青榮祿大夫，陞京東路行尚書省兼都緫帥，管領元附軍民，進金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Taizong appointed him overall commander of the Eastern Route, granted Silver-Green Grand Master of Glorious Blessings, advanced him to Eastern Jing Circuit Acting Ministry of Revenue Branch Secretariat and overall commander, overseeing newly submitted troops and civilians, and advanced him to Gold-Purple Grand Master of Glorious Blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong made him overall commander of the eastern route, granted him Silver-Green Grand Master of Glorious Blessings, then promoted him to head the eastern Jing branch secretariat with overall command over newly submitted troops and civilians, and finally to Gold-Purple Grand Master of Glorious Blessings.

sentences.zh: 庚子，賜金符。

translations.literal: In gengzi he was granted a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In 1240 he received a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 自兵興以來，子良轉徙南北，依之以全活者，不可勝計。

translations.literal: From the rise of warfare, as Ziliang shifted north and south, those who relied on him to survive entirely cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, countless people owed their survival to him as he moved back and forth across north and south.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，憲宗命為歸德府緫管，管領元附軍民。

translations.literal: In guichou Möngke appointed him intendant of Guide Prefecture, overseeing newly submitted troops and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: In 1253 Möngke appointed him intendant of Guide, with charge over newly submitted troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 中統二年夏四月，世祖命為歸德、泗州緫管，降虎符，仍管領泗州軍民緫管。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Zhongtong, Kublai appointed him intendant of Guide and Sizhou, granted a tiger tally, and still oversaw the Sizhou troops-and-civilians commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1261 Kublai made him intendant of Guide and Sizhou, gave him a tiger tally, and left him in charge of Sizhou's military and civilian administration.

sentences.zh: 七年，罷元管戶，隸諸郡縣，改授昭勇大將軍、大名路緫管，兼府尹。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the original registered households were abolished and placed under the various prefectures and counties; he was changed to Grand General of Manifest Courage and intendant of the Daming Circuit, concurrently prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the special household registers were abolished and subjects were placed under regular prefectures and counties; he was reassigned as Grand General of Manifest Courage, intendant of Daming, and concurrent prefect.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈昭勇大將軍、僉樞密院事、上輕車都尉，追封清河郡侯，諡翼敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Manifest Courage, commissioner of the Privy Council, Upper Light Chariot Commandant, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Qinghe with the posthumous title Yimin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand General of Manifest Courage, privy council commissioner, Upper Light Chariot Commandant, and Marquis of Qinghe with the posthumous title Yimin.

sentences.zh: 子二人：長懋，次亨。

translations.literal: He had two sons: the elder Mao, the younger Heng.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: the elder, Mao, and the younger, Heng.

sentences.zh: 亨，佩金虎符，為管軍千戶。

translations.literal: Heng wore a gold tiger tally and was commander of a thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Heng bore a gold tiger tally and served as commander of a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 子與立襲，卒。

translations.literal: His son Yuli inherited; he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuli inherited the post and later died.

sentences.zh: 子鑑襲。

translations.literal: His son Jian inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian inherited in turn.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，擢濟南諸路新軍千戶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan he was selected as thousand-household of the new army of the Jinan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1270 he was chosen as thousand-household of the new army on the Jinan circuits.

sentences.zh: 九年，從破襄樊有功。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed in breaking Xiangyang and Fancheng with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1272 he took part in the capture of Xiangyang and Fancheng with distinction.

sentences.zh: 十一年，丞相伯顏南征，其行陣以鏵車弩為先，而衆軍繼之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Chancellor Bayan campaigned south; his battle line took plow-cart crossbows first and the rest of the army followed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274, when Chancellor Bayan marched south, his van deployed plow-cart crossbows with the main force behind.

sentences.zh: 懋以勇鷙，將弩前行，凡所過山川道路險陿，通梁筏，平塹阱，安營設伏，出納奇計，伯顏信用之，擢為省都鎮撫，水陸並進，其任甚重。

translations.literal: Mao, for fierce courage, led the crossbows forward; wherever mountains, rivers, and roads were narrow and dangerous he built bridges and rafts, leveled pits and traps, set camps and ambushes, and offered unexpected plans—Bayan trusted and employed him, advanced him to secretariat overall pacification commissioner, advancing by land and water together in a role of very heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Mao, noted for fierce courage, led the crossbow units. Wherever the route was difficult he bridged streams, filled traps, set camps and ambushes, and offered bold plans. Bayan relied on him heavily, promoted him to overall pacification commissioner of the secretariat, and gave him a weighty role in the combined land and water advance.

sentences.zh: 師壓臨安，滅宋，以其主及母后群臣北還。

translations.literal: The army pressed Lin'an and extinguished Song; its ruler together with the empress dowager and the civil and military officials returned north.
translations.idiomatic: The army closed on Lin'an and destroyed the Song. The emperor, empress dowager, and court were sent north.

sentences.zh: 駐瓜洲，伯顏命懋往諭淮西夏貴，副以兩介，將騎士直趨合肥。

translations.literal: Encamped at Guazhou, Bayan ordered Mao to go announce to the Huai River's Xia noble, with two envoys as deputies, leading horsemen straight to Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: At Guazhou Bayan sent Mao to announce the new order to the Xia noble of the Huai region, with two envoys and a body of horsemen riding straight for Hefei.

sentences.zh: 貴出迎，設賓禮。

translations.literal: Gui came out to welcome him and set out guest rites.
translations.idiomatic: Gui came out to receive him with full ceremonial honors.

sentences.zh: 懋示以逆順禍福，辭旨雄厲，貴受命頓首，上地圖、降書。

translations.literal: Mao showed him the fortune and misfortune of obedience and rebellion; his words were forceful and stern; Gui received the command and bowed his head; he presented maps and a surrender document.
translations.idiomatic: Mao laid out the consequences of submission and resistance in stern, commanding language. Gui accepted the order, bowed, and presented maps and a written surrender.

sentences.zh: 馳還報，伯顏大喜。

translations.literal: He galloped back to report; Bayan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Mao rode back with the news, to Bayan's great delight.

sentences.zh: 復令行徇鎮巢、安豐、壽春、懷遠、淮安、濠等州郡，皆下。

translations.literal: Again he was ordered to tour and bring in Zhenchao, Anfeng, Shouchun, Huaiyuan, Huai'an, Hao, and other prefectures and districts—all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent again to bring in Zhenchao, Anfeng, Shouchun, Huaiyuan, Huai'an, Hao, and other prefectures, all of which submitted.

sentences.zh: 復使之遍諭列城軍民，使知帝之德意。

translations.literal: Again he was sent to announce broadly to the troops and civilians of the various cities so they would know the Emperor's virtuous intent.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent throughout the region to announce the emperor's benevolent intentions to soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 十三年，懋馳驛至上都，伯顏上其功，宣授懋明威將軍、泗州安撫司達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Mao rode post horses to the Upper Capital; Bayan reported his merit; by edict Mao was appointed General of Manifest Authority and darughachi of the Sizhou Pacification Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 Mao rode post relays to the Upper Capital. Bayan reported his merits, and an edict appointed him General of Manifest Authority and darughachi of the Sizhou pacification office.

sentences.zh: 十四年，改安撫司為緫管府，置宣慰使以統之，拜同知淮西道宣慰司事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the pacification office was changed to a directorate-general, a pacification commissioner was set to oversee it, and he was appointed associate commissioner of the Huaixi Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277 the pacification office became a directorate-general under a pacification commissioner, and Mao was made associate commissioner of the Huaixi pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 十六年，改授懷遠大將軍、吉州路緫管。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was changed to Grand General of Cherished Remoteness and intendant of the Jizhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1279 he was reassigned as Grand General of Cherished Remoteness and intendant of the Jizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 懋惡衣糲食，率之以儉，慎刑平政，處之以公，新府治，設義倉，雖能吏不過也。

translations.literal: Mao wore coarse clothes and ate plain food, leading others by frugality; he was careful in punishments and even in government, handling affairs with fairness; he built a new prefectural seat and established a charity granary—even able officials did not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Mao dressed plainly and ate simply, setting an example of thrift. He punished with care, governed equitably, rebuilt the prefectural offices, and founded a charity granary—surpassing even the ablest administrators.

sentences.zh: 部使者劉宣韙之，凡有所懲治，朝至夕報，豪強竦然。

translations.literal: The circuit inspector Liu Xuan praised him; whatever needed punishment was reported in the morning and answered by evening; the powerful shrank away.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit inspector Liu Xuan commended him. Cases requiring punishment were reported in the morning and resolved by evening, and the powerful quailed.

sentences.zh: 郡萬戶蘇良，恃勢為暴，為之翼者，有十虎之目，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: The prefectural ten-thousand-household Su Liang relied on power to act violently; those who aided him had the eyes of the Ten Tigers; the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural ten-thousand-household Su Liang bullied the people with his power. His henchmen were known as the Ten Tigers, and the populace suffered under them.

sentences.zh: 乃上其實於憲府，盡誅十虎者，奪良虎符而黜之，民大悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reported the facts to the surveillance commission; the Ten Tigers were all executed; Liang's tiger tally was seized and he was dismissed; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the facts to the surveillance commission. The Ten Tigers were all executed, Su Liang's tiger tally was taken and he was dismissed, and the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 群盜有率衆將白晝劫城者，懋聞之，率從騎擣其穴，縛其酋長以歸。

translations.literal: Among the bandit groups there were those who led crowds intending to plunder the city by daylight; when Mao heard of it he led his following horsemen to smash their den and bound their chiefs to bring back.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits gathered to raid the city in broad daylight, Mao led his escort in a raid on their hideout and brought back their chiefs bound.

sentences.zh: 民之流亡，與遠郡之來歸者數千家，相率為生祠以祀之。

translations.literal: Displaced people in flight and those coming to submit from distant prefectures numbered several thousand households; they together raised living shrines to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand refugee and submitter households raised living shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year he died, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of 1280 at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈昭勇大將軍、龍興路緫管、上輕車都尉，追封清河郡侯，諡宣敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand General of Manifest Courage, intendant of the Longxing Circuit, Upper Light Chariot Commandant, enfeoffed as Marquis of Qinghe, with the posthumous title Xuanmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand General of Manifest Courage, intendant of Longxing, Upper Light Chariot Commandant, and Marquis of Qinghe with the posthumous title Xuanmin.

sentences.zh: 子二人：文煥，以父蔭，任承務郎，江州路瑞昌縣尹。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Wenhuan, through his father's yin privilege, served as Court Gentleman for Meritorious Service and magistrate of Ruichang in Jiangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Wenhuan, who through his father's privilege held the rank of Court Gentleman for Meritorious Service and served as magistrate of Ruichang on the Jiangzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 文炳，三汊河巡檢。

translations.literal: Wenbing was inspector of the Sanhe River.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing served as inspector of the Sanhe River.

sentences.zh: 文煥子珪，初為高安縣尹，有異政，由是擢為江西檢校，拜南臺御史，繼為淮西、江西二道廉訪僉事，用能世其家云。

translations.literal: Wenhuan's son Gui at first was magistrate of Gao'an and had unusual administration; thereby he was selected as Jiangxi inspector, appointed Southern Terrace censor, and subsequently served as surveillance commissioner of the Huaixi and Jiangxi circuits—thus ability was passed down in the family.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan's son Gui first governed Gao'an with notable success, rose to Jiangxi inspector and Southern Terrace censor, and later became surveillance commissioner on the Huaixi and Jiangxi circuits, so the family's talent endured for generations.

sentences.zh: 唐慶，不知何許人，事太祖，為管軍萬戶。

translations.literal: Tang Qing—of unknown origin—served Taizu as commander of ten thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Qing, whose origins are unknown, served Taizu as a commander of ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 太祖伐金，以慶權元帥左監軍。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Jin he made Qing acting left overseer of the marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu attacked the Jin, he made Qing acting left overseer of the marshalate.

sentences.zh: 歲丁亥，賜虎符，授龍虎衛上將軍，使金。

translations.literal: In the year dinghai he was granted a tiger tally, appointed Grand General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, and sent to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1227 he received a tiger tally, was made Grand General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, and was sent as envoy to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，太宗復以慶為國信使，取金質子，督歲幣，以金曹王來，見帝於官山。

translations.literal: In renchen Taizong again made Qing an envoy of state trust, to take Jin hostages and supervise the annual tribute; the Jin Prince of Cao came and had audience with the Emperor at Guanshan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1232 Taizong again appointed Qing envoy of state trust to take Jin hostages and oversee the annual tribute. The Jin Prince of Cao came to audience with the emperor at Guanshan.

sentences.zh: 七月，使慶再往，令金主黜帝號稱臣，金主不聽，慶輒以語侵之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he sent Qing again, ordering the Jin ruler to remove the title of emperor and declare himself a subject; the Jin ruler would not listen, and Qing then used words to insult him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he sent Qing again with orders that the Jin ruler abandon the imperial title and submit as a vassal. When the Jin ruler refused, Qing insulted him openly.

sentences.zh: 金君臣遂謀害慶，夜半，令兵入館舍，殺慶，及其弟山祿、興祿，并從行者十七人。

translations.literal: Jin's ruler and ministers thereupon plotted to harm Qing; at midnight they ordered troops into the hostel, killed Qing, and his younger brothers Shanlu and Xinglu, together with seventeen of those who followed on the mission.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court then plotted his murder. At midnight soldiers entered the hostel and killed Qing, his brothers Shanlu and Xinglu, and seventeen members of his mission.

sentences.zh: 既滅金，購求慶屍不得，厚恤其家，賜金五十斤，詔官其子，仍計其家人口，給糧以養焉。

translations.literal: After Jin was extinguished they sought Qing's corpse but could not obtain it; they generously comforted his family, granted fifty jin of gold, ordered officials to enfeoff his sons, and still counted his household members to give grain for their support.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin fell they could not recover his body. The court richly compensated his family with fifty jin of gold, enfeoffed his sons by edict, and allotted grain according to the number of his household members.

sentences.zh: 齊榮顯

translations.literal: Qi Rongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Rongxian

sentences.zh: 齊榮顯字仁卿，聊城人。

translations.literal: Qi Rongxian, courtesy name Renqing, was a man of Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Rongxian, whose courtesy name was Renqing, came from Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 父旺，金同知山東西路兵馬都緫管。

translations.literal: His father Wang was Jin associate commissioner of the Shandong West Route horse-and-foot overall command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang had been Jin associate commissioner of the Shandong Western Route overall command of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 榮顯幼聰悟，緫角與群兒戲，畫地為戰陣，端坐指揮，各就行列。

translations.literal: Rongxian in youth was clever and perceptive; when his hair was still unbound he played with the group of children, drew the ground as a battle array, sat upright directing, and each went to his rank.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Rongxian was quick-witted. While still a child he would draw battle lines on the ground for his playmates and sit directing them into formation.

sentences.zh: 九歲，代父任為千戶，佩金符，從外舅嚴實來歸，屢立戰功。

translations.literal: At nine years he replaced his father as thousand-household, wore a gold tally, followed his maternal uncle Yan Shi in submitting, and repeatedly established battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: At nine he succeeded his father as thousand-household with a gold tally, followed his maternal uncle Yan Shi in submission, and won repeated distinction in battle.

sentences.zh: 攻濠州，宋兵背城為陣，榮顯薄之，所向披靡。

translations.literal: Attacking Haozhou, Song troops with their backs to the city formed a battle line; Rongxian pressed them and wherever he went they were scattered.
translations.idiomatic: At Haozhou the Song drew up with their backs to the wall. Rongxian pressed the line and broke whatever he touched.

sentences.zh: 其屬王孝忠力戰，中鉤戟，榮顯斷戟拔孝忠出，復逐北，入其郛而還。

translations.literal: His subordinate Wang Xiaozhong fought fiercely, was struck by a hook-spear; Rongxian severed the spear and pulled Xiaozhong out, again pursued north, entered their outer wall and returned.
translations.idiomatic: His man Wang Xiaozhong fought hard and was caught by a hooked halberd. Rongxian cut the weapon free, pulled him out, drove the enemy back, and entered their outer defenses before returning.

sentences.zh: 主帥察罕壯之，賜馬鎧銀器。

translations.literal: Commander Chaghan admired this and granted horse, armor, and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Chaghan admired his feat and rewarded him with a horse, armor, and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 兵趨五河口，抵大堤，榮顯偕數騎前行覘敵，值邏騎數十，從者將退走，榮顯曰：「彼衆我寡，若示以怯，必為所乘。」

translations.literal: The army pressed toward Wuhekou and reached the great embankment; Rongxian with several horsemen went forward to scout the enemy and met several tens of patrol horsemen; his followers were about to retreat and flee; Rongxian said: "They are many, we few—if we show fear we will surely be overcome by them."
